item.title: Starmer to face Commons over Mandelson vetting scandal
item.description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer is set to address the House of Commons on Monday in what is being described as a fight for his political survival, as he seeks to explain how Peter Mandelson was appointed as ambassador to the United States despite having failed security vetting — a fact Starmer insists was concealed from him by Foreign Office officials.

item.title: Israel, Lebanon to hold second round of talks in Washington on Thursday
item.description:
Israel and Lebanon are set to hold a second round of ambassador-level talks in Washington on Thursday, April 23, according to Israeli media reports, marking the first direct diplomatic contact between the two countries since a 10-day ceasefire took effect on April 16.

The meeting, expected to be hosted at the U.S. State Department, follows a first round held on April 14 that was widely described as historic — the highest-level direct engagement between Israel and Lebanon since 1993. That session, chaired by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, lasted more than two hours and included Israeli Ambassador Yechiel Leiter, Lebanese Ambassador Nada Hamadeh Moawad, and other U.S. officials.

item.title: Starmer admits misleading Parliament over Mandelson vetting scandal
item.description:
British Prime Minister Keir Starmer addressed a hostile House of Commons on Monday, admitting that he had misled Parliament over the failed security vetting of Lord Peter Mandelson — but insisted the error was inadvertent.

Starmer told lawmakers he should never have appointed Mandelson as the United Kingdom's ambassador to Washington, acknowledging a catastrophic lapse that has now engulfed his premiership and drawn resignation calls from all major opposition parties.

item.title: Apple names John Ternus CEO as Tim Cook shifts to chairman role
item.description:
Apple announced on Monday that John Ternus, the company's senior vice president of hardware engineering, will become its next chief executive officer effective September 1, replacing Tim Cook, who will transition to the role of executive chairman of the board. The move, approved unanimously by Apple's board of directors, caps months of intensifying succession speculation and marks only the third CEO transition in Apple's 50-year history.

Cook will remain as CEO through the summer to work closely with Ternus on the handover. As executive chairman, Cook will continue to assist the company, including engaging with policymakers around the world. Arthur Levinson, Apple's non-executive chairman for the past 15 years, will become the board's lead independent director on the same date.

item.title: Iraq, Syria reopen Rabia border crossing after 13 years
item.description: Iraq and Syria on Monday officially reopened the Rabia-Al Yarubiyah border crossing, restoring a trade and transit route that had been shuttered for nearly 13 years amid civil war and the rise of ISIS. The reopening makes all official border crossings between the two countries operational for the first time since conflict engulfed the region.

item.title: LHC experiment finds high-significance crack in the Standard Model
item.description: Physicists working on the Large Hadron Collider at CERN in Geneva have reported a measurement that deviates from the predictions of the Standard Model of particle physics by four standard deviations — a result that, if confirmed, could represent the first crack in the theory that has dominated the field for half a century.

item.title: Iran warns of 'new cards on the battlefield' as ceasefire nears expiration
item.description: Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned on Monday that Tehran has prepared to "reveal new cards on the battlefield" if war with the United States resumes, as a two-week ceasefire approaches its Wednesday expiration with no deal in sight and negotiations in disarray.

item.title: Iran warns of 'new cards on the battlefield' as ceasefire nears end
item.description: Iran's Parliament Speaker and top negotiator Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf declared on Monday that Tehran will not negotiate with the United States under coercion, accusing President Donald Trump of trying to turn the negotiating table into "a table of surrender." His remarks came as the ceasefire between the two countries neared its expiration and uncertainty mounted over whether a second round of peace talks would take place.

item.title: Oil prices surge as US-Iran ceasefire nears expiration
item.description: Oil prices swung sharply on Monday as escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz collided with uncertainty over whether the United States and Iran would sit down for a second round of peace talks before a ceasefire expires on Wednesday.

item.title: Asian markets trade mixed as U.S.-Iran ceasefire set to expire Tuesday night
item.description:
Oil prices dipped and Asian stock markets traded in mixed fashion on Tuesday as uncertainty deepened over the fate of peace negotiations between the United States and Iran, with a two-week ceasefire set to expire Tuesday evening Eastern time.

Brent crude slipped 0.4% while U.S. benchmark crude fell 0.9% in early Asian trading, according to the Associated Press. The declines came as traders weighed the possibility of fresh diplomatic talks in Islamabad against rising tensions, including the U.S. Navy's recent seizure of an Iranian cargo vessel in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Clean energy outpaced global electricity demand growth in 2025, Ember finds
item.description:
Clean energy generation outpaced global electricity demand growth for the first time in 2025, powered by record solar expansion in China and India, according to energy think tank Ember's Global Electricity Review 2026, released on Monday.

Clean power generation grew 887 terawatt hours last year, exceeding overall global electricity demand growth of 849 terawatt hours, the report found. Solar energy, which grew 30% in 2025, alone met three-quarters of the net rise in electricity demand, and combined with wind power generation, met 99% of it.

item.title: Oil dips as Iran agrees to join U.S. peace talks in Islamabad
item.description: Oil prices fell on Tuesday as expectations grew that the United States and Iran would resume peace negotiations in Pakistan this week, raising hopes for an easing of supply disruptions in the Middle East. The decline came after a volatile Monday session that saw crude surge on renewed tensions over the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: SpaceX begins Wall Street analyst briefings ahead of record $75B IPO
item.description:
SpaceX kicked off three days of private analyst meetings on Monday at its Starbase launch site in Boca Chica, Texas, as Elon Musk's rocket and satellite company moves closer to what would be the largest initial public offering in history, Reuters reported.

The briefings, aimed at Wall Street's top aerospace and technology analysts, mark a key milestone in SpaceX's push to raise up to $75 billion and begin trading by late June. Executives are expected to lead an all-day meeting and tour at Starbase before offering analysts a visit to SpaceX's "Macrohard" xAI datacenter in Memphis, Tennessee, on April 23.

item.title: Japan scraps postwar ban on lethal weapons exports
item.description: Japan's Cabinet on Tuesday approved the most sweeping overhaul of the country's defense export rules in decades, scrapping restrictions that had confined arms sales to non-combat equipment since the end of World War II. The decision opens the door for Japanese manufacturers to sell fighter jets, missiles, warships, and other lethal weapons on the global market for the first time.

item.title: Rio Tinto posts higher Q1 iron ore sales, warns on Middle East risks
item.description: Rio Tinto reported a 2.4% rise in first-quarter iron ore sales on Tuesday but cautioned that the ongoing conflict in the Middle East could disrupt its supply chains in the second half of 2026. The world's largest iron ore producer sold 72.4 million metric tons from its Pilbara operations in Western Australia during the three months ended March 31, up from 70.7 million tons a year earlier, though below the Visible Alpha consensus estimate of 74.6 million tons.

item.title: Airbus agrees to acquire French cybersecurity firm Quarkslab
item.description: Airbus announced on Monday that it has entered into an agreement to acquire Quarkslab, a French cybersecurity company, in a deal that extends the European aerospace giant's push to build sovereign cyber capabilities across the continent.

item.title: Trump's Board of Peace in talks with DP World on Gaza rebuild
item.description: Representatives of Donald Trump's Board of Peace have held discussions with Dubai-based logistics giant DP World about managing supply chains and infrastructure projects in Gaza, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday, in a move that underscores Washington's push to privatise key elements of the territory's rebuilding effort.

item.title: Curiosity rover detects 'origin-of-life' molecules on Mars
item.description: NASA's Curiosity rover has detected more than 20 organic molecules in clay-rich Martian rock, including compounds never before seen on the Red Planet, according to a study published on April 21 in the journal Nature Communications. The findings, drawn from a first-of-its-kind chemical experiment conducted remotely on Mars, offer fresh clues in the decades-long search for signs of ancient life beyond Earth.

item.title: UN climate chief warns of fossil-fuel stagflation at Berlin talks
item.description: UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell warned on Tuesday that "fossil-fuel driven stagflation is now stalking economies," urging nations to accelerate clean energy adoption as the primary defense against rising temperatures and volatile energy costs. Speaking at the opening of the Petersberg Climate Dialogue in Berlin on April 21, Stiell described climate cooperation as essential to "fending off the twin-reapers of global heating and fossil fuel cost chaos."

item.title: Seized Iranian ship Touska likely carried dual-use cargo, sources say
item.description: U.S. naval forces attacked and seized the Iranian-flagged cargo ship MV Touska on April 19 after a six-hour standoff in the Gulf of Oman, marking the first such enforcement action since the United States imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports on April 13. Iran condemned the seizure as "maritime piracy" and vowed military retaliation, pulling out of planned peace talks in Pakistan and casting doubt on a fragile ceasefire set to expire on April 21.
